ramesey-retain-money.locator: Liber III, second-house elections, chapter II, p.135: received money remaining long
ramesey-retain-money.interpretation: For retaining received money, the cited passage requests fixed signs for the Ascendant, its lord, Moon, second lord and angles.

ramesey-rapid-use-money.locator: Liber III, second-house elections, chapter II, pp.135–136: speedily disbursing money
ramesey-rapid-use-money.interpretation: For rapid circulation the passage prefers movable signs. Common signs are an admitted alternative, not included in this narrow preferred-sign profile.

asc-ruler-direct.locator: Liber III, introductory chapter I, p.124: Ascendant lord retrogradation

diagnostics.method: Report whether the Moon occupies the first house.

diagnostics.locator: pp.124–125: angular malefics, benefics and event significators
diagnostics.method: Report angular benefics/malefics without assuming natural benefic/malefic status settles event-specific function.
Report instantaneous applying aspects with an explicit operational orb; do not claim next perfection or absence of prohibition.
Expose Moon, Ascendant lord and second lord dignities/debilities, retrogradation, solar proximity and reception; no invented fortification score.

source_conflicts.scope: Borrowing/lending, not the implemented retention/circulation categories
source_conflicts.locator: chapter I p.135 versus chapter II Haly discussion
positions: Ramesey first rejects lending/borrowing under specified first-degree signs.
He then records Haly's distinction favoring borrower over lender in such cases.
source_conflicts.resolution: Recorded, not averaged or applied to an unrelated category.
